subject: Multivariate lm.rrpp with multivariate independent variables

messages.author: 544eca9c804a0347
messages.subject: Multivariate lm.rrpp with multivariate independent variables
parts:
Dear colleagues,

recently I have been wondering if it might be possible to explain (multivariate) variation in coordinates with another set of coordinates (specifically the coordinates/shape from each individual's father). After conducting a gpa on paternal coordinates and merging datasets, I have been trying to do that:

fit <- lm.rrpp(coords ~ fathercoords, SS.type = "II", data=dat.full, iter=9999)

However, this analysis does not go through, and errors out with
ERROR: One or more independent variables does not match the number
of observations in the data.

Looking at the data structure, the number of observations seem to match perfectly, though.

str(dat.full)
List of 2
 $ coords      : num [1:14000, 1:26] 0.408 0.402 0.397 0.407 0.402 ...
  ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
  .. ..$ : chr [1:14000] "0 " "1 " "2 " "3 " ...
  .. ..$ : chr [1:26] "1.X" "1.Y" "2.X" "2.Y" ...
 $ fathercoords: num [1:14000, 1:26] 0.391 0.391 0.391 0.391 0.391 ...
  ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
  .. ..$ : chr [1:14000] "1 " "1 " "1 " "1 " ...
  .. ..$ : chr [1:26] "1.X" "1.Y" "2.X" "2.Y" ...
 - attr(*, "class")= chr "geomorph.data.frame"

Thus I suspect that lm.rrpp does not support multivariate independent variables. Or am I overlooking something here?

Thank you for your time!

Cheers
Bob

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Multivariate lm.rrpp with multivariate independent variables
parts:
There is nothing wrong with lm.rrpp: it works fine with multiple independent variables. What you are doing however makes no sense. Partial least squares is how one should investigate such covariation.

 

I suggest you read more carefully the general theory papers in morphometrics and multivariate statistics prior to embarking on such code-based experiments. A deeper knowledge of these components will enlighten how one can ask certain questions, and generally facilitate progress. Next, a careful examination of help files and vignettes that come with the software will demonstrate proper use.

 

All of these will lighten the load of questions that the community is receiving, and can lead to more productive outcomes.

 

Dean
